question: P can do a piece of work in 48 days and Q and do half of the same work in 30 days. If they both work together, in how many days can they complete three - eigth of the work?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Work = LCM(48, 60) = 240 units.

Efficiency of P = 240 ÷ 48 = 5 units/day.

Efficiency of Q = 240 ÷ (30 × 2) = 4 units/day.

Target Work = 3/8 × 240 = 90 units.

Required Time = 90 ÷ (5 + 4) = 10 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by P to complete the work = 48 days.

Time taken by Q to complete half of the work = 30 days.

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Efficiency × Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Time taken by Q to complete the full work = 30 × 2 = 60 days.

⇒ Combined efficiency of P and Q = 5 + 4 = 9 units/day.

⇒ Target work = 3/8 of 240 = 3/8 × 240 = 90 units.

⇒ Time taken by P and Q together = Target work ÷ Combined efficiency.

⇒ Time taken = 90 ÷ 9 = 10 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns

Similar to Time & Work, where the total capacity acts as total work. Filling pipe efficiency is positive, while an emptying pipe (leak) efficiency is negative.

Work and Wages

Wages are strictly divided in the ratio of the total work done. If people work for the same number of days, the wage ratio is directly equal to their efficiency ratio.

Alternate Day Work

Calculate the work completed in one cycle (e.g., A works day 1, B works day 2). Find the maximum whole cycles that fit into the total work, then assign the remaining work to the first person.
